topic.title: Ensemble Diversity, Calibration, and Adaptive Inference
topic.overview: Ensembles combine predictors to improve decisions, but their benefits depend on the quality and genuine complementarity of members. This topic studies diversity, uncertainty, distribution shift, and efficient execution. Representative work questions whether apparent disagreement generalizes and whether a larger single model can reproduce benefits attributed to ensembling.
topic.whyItMatters: Training several models costs more, and diversity metrics can reward differences that do not help on new data. Useful ensembles need evaluation against equally capable alternatives and procedures that spend additional computation only when it improves the decision.
topic.evolution: Early papers examine accurate, diverse members and bagging-like methods. Later work studies hyperparameter ensembles and uncertainty-aware selection. Recent analyses expose collusion under joint training and qualify robustness claims, while adaptive stacking-and-cascading methods seek ensemble quality without evaluating every member for every input.
openQuestions: How can training encourage diversity that remains useful out of distribution?
When is another ensemble prediction more valuable than allocating compute to one stronger model?
